scientific_center: joint developmental calibration of speaker effort and fixed-effort form predictability

eligibility.reason: A child-specific developmental slope and a three-dimensional session-clustered covariance cannot be stably estimated from three sessions.

scaling.entropy_reference: all-79 mean and SD inherited from the audited source

estimands.label: developmental change in demand sensitivity
estimands.unit: change in the entropy slope per six months

joint_model.formula: coefficient_hat_child[3] ~ MVN(theta_child[3], known_session_clustered_cov_child); theta_child ~ MVN(mu + corpus_effect, Sigma_child)
joint_model.interpretation: coordinated development, not optimization or causality

priors.source: effect-scale regularization; PBM estimates are not used as priors

diagnostic_gates.note: Influence refits use half-length chains and are posterior-mean stress tests, not separate inferential fits. All-parameter diagnostics remain saved.

interpretation_guardrails: This is a post-hoc joint extension; the underlying outcomes were inspected previously.
PBM is a discovery label, not a Bayesian prior.
Corpus is background hierarchical structure, not the scientific focus.
Lower k3 surprisal means greater scorer predictability or conventionality, not greater Shannon information transmitted.
Exact-string response entropy is generator-, prompt-, temperature-, and surface-form-dependent.
The Route 2 coefficient describes log(1 + words), not listener benefit.
Cross-child correlations indicate coordinated developmental variation, not optimization or causality.
A strong communicative-efficiency claim remains contingent on the downstream caregiver-response utility analysis.
